# prolfqua - a comprehensive R package for Proteomics Differential Expression Analysis

![prolfqua hex sticker](reference/figures/imgfile.png)

The R package contains functions for analysing mass spectrometry based
experiments. It is intended for proteomics core facilities and
researchers who analyse label-free protein or peptide intensities
quantified with MaxQuant, DIA-NN, Spectronaut, FragPipe or similar
software. This package is developed at the [FGCZ](https://fgcz.ch/). The
package documentation including vignettes can be accessed at
<https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/index.html>

`prolfqua` makes easy things easy while remaining fully hackable.

At its centre is a factory,
[`build_contrast_analysis()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/build_contrast_analysis.md):
one call fits a model per protein and computes the requested contrasts.
The `method` argument selects one of 20 models, and every model returns
its results through the same interface. Start with the [Introduction to
prolfqua](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/articles/prolfqua.html).

![build_contrast_analysis() as a factory rolling out all modelling
methods](reference/figures/prolfqua_factory.png)

# Statement of need

Label-free quantification (LFQ) experiments measure thousands of
proteins or peptides in few samples, and values go missing more often at
low intensity. Methods for their differential expression analysis are
spread over packages with different input formats, model specifications
and outputs (limma, DEqMS, MSstats, msqrob2, proDA, limpa), which makes
it hard to choose a method for a dataset or to compare methods on it.

prolfqua gives these methods one data model, a long table with an
`AnalysisConfiguration` naming the column roles; one model
specification, R’s formula interface including mixed models; and one
output format.
[`build_contrast_analysis()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/build_contrast_analysis.md)
fits any of its 20 methods and returns contrasts with the same columns,
so a core facility can run, compare and report them in one workflow, and
a researcher can check how much a result depends on the method. prolfqua
also covers the steps around the test: quality control, normalisation,
aggregation of peptides to proteins and sample-size estimation.

# How to install prolfqua?

prolfqua requires R (\>= 4.6); check your version with
`R.version.string` and update R first if needed.

prolfqua is part of
[Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/prolfqua/) from release
3.24. To install the Bioconductor release:

``` r
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("prolfqua")
```

If BiocManager reports that prolfqua is not available for your
Bioconductor version, update Bioconductor with
`BiocManager::install(version = "3.24")` and run
`BiocManager::install("prolfqua")` again.

Bioconductor publishes a release every six months. The development
version on GitHub has the changes made since then, listed in the
[changelog](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/news/index.html). Installing
it from GitHub needs the remotes package:

``` r
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install("fgcz/prolfqua")
```

`packageVersion("prolfqua")` shows which version you have installed.

Some methods and plots use packages listed under `Suggests`; prolfqua
asks to install them when they are needed.

Let us please know about any installation problems or errors when using
the package: <https://github.com/fgcz/prolfqua/issues>

# How to get started

How to build a `LFQData` object from a table with protein or peptide
quantification results, and a table with sample annotation is described
in more detail in the [Importing your data
vignette](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/articles/CreatingConfigurations.html).

A minimal example for a table with protein abundances is:

``` r
# Table with abundances
df <- data.frame(
  protein_Id = c("tr|A|HUMAN", "tr|B|HUMAN", "tr|C|HUMAN", "tr|D|HUMAN"),
  Intensity_A = c(100, 10000, 10, NA),
  Intensity_B = c(NA, 9000, 20, 100),
  Intensity_C = c(200, 8000, NA, 150),
  Intensity_D = c(130, 11000, 50, 50)
)
# Table with sample annotation
annot <- data.frame(
  Sample = c("Intensity_A", "Intensity_B", "Intensity_C", "Intensity_D"),
  Group = c("A", "A", "B", "C")
)

# convert into long format
table_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(df, dplyr::starts_with("Intensity_"), names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Intensity")
table_long <- dplyr::inner_join(annot, table_long, by = "Sample")
# peptides per protein and sample; used as weights by some methods (1 if unknown)
table_long$nr_children <- 1L

# create the AnalysisConfiguration
config <- prolfqua::AnalysisConfiguration$new()
config$file_name <- "Sample"
config$work_intensity <- "Intensity"
config$hierarchy[["protein_Id"]] <- "protein_Id"
config$factors[["Group"]] <- "Group"

# Build LFQData object
analysis_data <- prolfqua::setup_analysis(table_long, config)
#> creating sampleName from file_name column
#> no identification_confidence column specified in the data, adding it and setting the identification confidence to 1.
#> setup_analysis: derived identification_confidence_feature, nr_children_feature as the maximum over samples.
lfqdata <- prolfqua::LFQData$new(analysis_data, config)
lfqdata$hierarchy_counts()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>   protein_Id
#>        <int>
#> 1          4
```

Once you have created an `LFQData` you can use prolfqua like this.

``` r
library(prolfqua)

## here we simulate peptide level data
startdata <- sim_lfq_data_peptide_config()
lfqpep <- LFQData$new(startdata$data, startdata$config)

## transform intensities and aggregate peptides to proteins
lfqpep <- lfqpep$get_Transformer()$log2()$robscale()$lfq
lfqpep$rename_response("log_peptide_abundance")
agr <- lfqpep$get_Aggregator()
lfqpro <- agr$aggregate()
lfqpro$rename_response("log_protein_abundance")

## plot Figure 3 panels A-D
pl <- lfqpep$get_Plotter()
panelA <- pl$intensity_distribution_density() +
  ggplot2::labs(tag = "A") + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
panelB <- agr$plot()$plots[[1]] + ggplot2::labs(tag = "B")
panelC <- lfqpro$get_Stats()$violin() + ggplot2::labs(tag = "C")
pl <- lfqpro$get_Plotter()
panelD <- pl$boxplots()$boxplot[[1]] + ggplot2::labs(tag = "D")
gridExtra::grid.arrange(panelA, panelB, panelC, panelD)
```

![Peptide intensity densities, peptide-to-protein aggregation, standard
deviations per group, and protein
boxplot](reference/figures/README-overview-1.png)

``` r
## specify contrasts
Contr <- c(
  "AvsCtrl" = "group_A - group_Ctrl",
  "BvsCtrl" = "group_B - group_Ctrl",
  "BvsA" = "group_B - group_A"
)

## fit a model per protein and compute the contrasts, here with limma
fa <- build_contrast_analysis(lfqpro, "~ group_", Contr, method = "limma")
#> fit (limma): 4 missing responses dropped (e.g. 7cbcrd~5725, 9VUkAq~4703, CGzoYe~2147): NA response (missing observation) left out of the fit
#> See $provenance().
head(fa$get_contrasts())
#> # A tibble: 6 × 16
#>   modelName estimate_type protein_Id  contrast    diff        FDR
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr>       <chr>      <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 limma     observed      0EfVhX~0087 AvsCtrl  -0.0506 0.485     
#> 2 limma     observed      7cbcrd~5725 AvsCtrl   0.707  0.00000378
#> 3 limma     observed      9VUkAq~4703 AvsCtrl  -0.593  0.00000378
#> 4 limma     observed      BEJI92~5282 AvsCtrl   0.273  0.0146    
#> 5 limma     observed      CGzoYe~2147 AvsCtrl  -0.231  0.00391   
#> 6 limma     observed      DoWup2~5896 AvsCtrl   0.266  0.00391   
#> # ℹ 10 more variables: std.error.unmoderated <dbl>, df.unmoderated <dbl>,
#> #   std.error <dbl>, statistic <dbl>, p.value <dbl>, sigma <dbl>, df <dbl>,
#> #   conf.low <dbl>, conf.high <dbl>, avgAbd <dbl>

## volcano plot
fa$get_Plotter()$volcano()$FDR
```

![Volcano plots of the three contrasts, -log10(FDR) against log2 fold
change](reference/figures/README-volcano-1.png)

# Design

The package for **pro**teomics **l**abel **f**ree **qua**ntification
`prolfqua` (read: prolevka) evolved from scripts written at the FGCZ to
visualise and analyse mass spectrometry data; some of them are still in
the R packages quantable, protViz and imsbInfer.

prolfqua stores the data in one table in long format, with an
`AnalysisConfiguration` naming the column roles: the hierarchy (for
example protein and peptide), the explanatory factors, the sample and
the response. Data in long format, as written by Spectronaut, Skyline or
DIA-NN, needs only this configuration; wide matrices, as written by
MaxQuant, are converted with
[`lfqdata_from_wide()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/lfqdata_from_wide.md),
and the [prolfquapp](https://github.com/prolfqua/prolfquapp) package
reads the output of common quantification software. Results are data
frames, so dplyr and ggplot2 work on every step.

Models are specified with R’s formula interface, including lme4 formulas
for mixed models, so parallel, factorial and repeated-measurement
designs need no special code. On top of the model fits, prolfqua
implements p-value moderation as in limma, the peptide-median
aggregation of PECA and ROPECA, and refits at the limit of detection for
groups without observations, which makes these methods comparable within
one framework. Besides differential expression, prolfqua computes
coefficients of variation, estimates sample sizes, summarises missing
values and intensity distributions, aggregates peptides to proteins (top
N, Tukey’s median polish, robust regression) and compares models with
likelihood ratio tests.

To use `prolfqua`, knowledge of R’s regression model infrastructure is
an advantage.

## Related projects

- prolfquabenchmark - a package to document the performance of prolfqua,
  MSstats, msqrob2, and proDA. See documentation:
  <https://prolfqua.github.io/prolfquabenchmark/>
- prolfquapp: Generating Dynamic DEA Reports with the prolfqua R Package
  <https://github.com/prolfqua/prolfquapp>
- prophosqua - (scripts for the analysis of phospho experiments)
  <https://github.com/prolfqua/prophosqua>

## Related packages

- [limma](https://bioconductor.org/packages/limma/) and
  [DEqMS](https://bioconductor.org/packages/DEqMS/): moderated t-tests
  on a protein matrix; prolfqua’s `limma`, `limma_voom` and `deqms`
  methods call them
- [limpa](https://bioconductor.org/packages/limpa/): detection
  probability curve and precision weights; prolfqua’s `limpa` methods
  call it
- [PECA](https://bioconductor.org/packages/PECA/): peptide-median
  aggregation (PECA, ROPECA); prolfqua’s `ropeca_nested` is derived from
  it
- [MSstats](https://bioconductor.org/packages/MSstats/): protein
  summarisation and linear mixed models
- [msqrob2](https://bioconductor.org/packages/msqrob2/): robust ridge
  regression on peptide or protein level, built on QFeatures
- [proDA](https://bioconductor.org/packages/proDA/): probabilistic
  dropout model, inference without imputation
- [DAPAR](https://bioconductor.org/packages/DAPAR/) and
  [DAPARdata](https://bioconductor.org/packages/DAPARdata/): imputation
  and statistical analysis behind the Prostar interface
- [Triqler](https://github.com/statisticalbiotechnology/triqler):
  Bayesian error propagation from identification to quantification
  (Python)

## R packages to compute contrasts from linear and other models

- [marginaleffects](https://marginaleffects.com/) Compute and plot
  predictions, slopes, marginal means, and comparisons (contrasts, risk
  ratios, odds ratios, etc.) for over 70 classes of statistical models
  in R.
- [emmeans](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=emmeans) Obtain estimated
  marginal means (EMMs) for many linear, generalized linear, and mixed
  models.
- [lmerTest](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=lmerTest) computes
  contrast for [lme4](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=lme4) models
- [multcomp](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=multcomp) computes
  contrast for linear models and adjusts p-values (multiple comparison)

## Relevant background information

- [R Companion](https://rcompanion.org/rcompanion/h_01.html)
- [Extending the Linear Model with
  R](https://www.maths.bath.ac.uk/~jjf23/ELM/)

  Maier](https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/65059_586f394d8eb84f84b1baaf56ffb6b47f.html)
- [Interactions and Contrasts PH525x
  series](https://genomicsclass.github.io/book/pages/interactions_and_contrasts.html)

# Package index

## Differential expression analysis

One call fits a model per protein and tests the contrasts; each method
is a facade class.

- [`build_contrast_analysis()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/build_contrast_analysis.md)
  : Build a contrast analysis using one of several statistical methods
- [`print(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`confint(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`formula(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`nobs(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`fitted(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`predict(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`residuals(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  [`plot(`*`<ContrastsFacadeBase>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/prolfqua_analysis_methods.md)
  : Inspect a fitted prolfqua analysis
- [`list_facades()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/list_facades.md)

  : DEqMS contrast analysis facade

  : Rfit rank-based regression contrast analysis facade
- [`ContrastsRfitImputeFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsRfitImputeFacade.md)
  : Rfit rank-regression contrast analysis with LOD imputation facade

  : Merge contrast results coming from two different model.
- [`pivot_model_contrasts_to_wide()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/pivot_model_contrasts_to_wide.md)
  : Pivot long-format model contrasts to wide format
- [`impute_from_model()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/impute_from_model.md)
  : Fill missing responses with predictions from per-subject linear

## Data container

LFQData and the objects returned by its get\_ methods.

- [`AggregateLimpa`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/AggregateLimpa.md)
  : Aggregate or impute intensities with limpa's DPC quantification
- [`AggregateMedpolish`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/AggregateMedpolish.md)
  : Aggregate peptide intensities by median polish
- [`AggregateRlm`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/AggregateRlm.md)
  : Aggregate peptide intensities by robust linear regression
- [`AggregateTopN`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/AggregateTopN.md)
  : Aggregate peptide intensities from the top N peptides
- [`LFQData`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/LFQData.md) :
  LFQData R6 class
- [`LFQDataPlotter`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/LFQDataPlotter.md)
  : Plot LFQData
- [`LFQDataStats`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/LFQDataStats.md)
  : Decorates LFQData with methods to compute statistics of interactions
- [`LFQDataSummariser`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/LFQDataSummariser.md)
  : Summarize LFQData
- [`lfqdata_from_wide()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/lfqdata_from_wide.md)
  : Build LFQData from wide matrices
- [`lfqdata_to_summarized_experiment()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/lfqdata_to_summarized_experiment.md)
  : Convert an LFQData object to a SummarizedExperiment
- [`plot(`*`<LFQData>`*`)`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/plot.LFQData.md)
  : Plot an LFQData object
- [`LFQDataTransformer`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/LFQDataTransformer.md)
  : Decorate LFQData with Methods for transforming Intensities
- [`MissingHelpers`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/MissingHelpers.md)
  : Group statistics and limit of detection

## Contrast definitions

- [`annotation_add_contrasts()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/annotation_add_contrasts.md)
  : Add the contrasts of a two-factor design to a sample annotation
- [`generate_contrasts()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/generate_contrasts.md)
  : All contrasts of a two-factor design
- [`generate_contrasts_for_factor()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/generate_contrasts_for_factor.md)
  : Pairwise contrasts of one factor
- [`interaction_contrasts()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/interaction_contrasts.md)
  : Interaction contrasts of a two-factor design
- [`level_specific_contrasts()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/level_specific_contrasts.md)
  : Level-specific contrasts of a two-factor design
- [`main_effect_contrasts()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/main_effect_contrasts.md)
  : Main-effect contrasts of a two-factor design

## Models, strategies and contrasts

The steps behind the facades, for inspecting or changing one of them.

- [`AnovaExtractor`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/AnovaExtractor.md)
  : R6 class for extracting ANOVA results as a data frame
- [`Contrasts`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/Contrasts.md)
  : Estimate contrasts using Wald Test
- [`ContrastsComparison`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsComparison.md)
  : Compare the contrasts of several methods on their subject and
  contrast pairs
- [`ContrastsDEqMSFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsDEqMSFacade.md)
  : DEqMS contrast analysis facade
- [`ContrastsDEqMSVoomFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsDEqMSVoomFacade.md)
  : DEqMS contrast analysis with vooma weights facade
- [`ContrastsFacadeBase`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsFacadeBase.md)
  : Base class for contrast analysis facades
- [`ContrastsFirth`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsFirth.md)
  : Contrasts of Firth logistic regression models
- [`ContrastsFirthFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsFirthFacade.md)
  : Firth logistic missingness contrast analysis facade
- [`ContrastsHurdleFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsHurdleFacade.md)
  : Hurdle contrasts: intensity and detection combined with Fisher's
  method
- [`ContrastsHurdleNestedFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsHurdleNestedFacade.md)
  : Hurdle contrast facade for nested input
- [`ContrastsLMFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsLMFacade.md)
  : LM contrast analysis facade
- [`ContrastsLMImputeFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsLMImputeFacade.md)
  : LM contrast analysis with LOD imputation facade
- [`ContrastsLimma`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsLimma.md)
  : Limma-based contrasts (direct limma pipeline)
- [`ContrastsLimmaFacade`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/ContrastsLimmaFacade.md)
  : Limma contrast analysis facade

## Statistics and sample size

- [`fdr_sig_level()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/fdr_sig_level.md)
  : Per-test significance level for FDR-controlled sample-size planning
- [`null_split_check()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/null_split_check.md)
  : Null-split calibration check of normalization and model
- [`pooled_variance_explained()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/pooled_variance_explained.md)
  : Variance explained by each term, pooled over features
- [`power_fdr_prior_n()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/power_fdr_prior_n.md)
  : Plan sample size from a pilot variance prior and a planned effect
  distribution
- [`summarize_variance_explained()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/summarize_variance_explained.md)
  : Variance explained by the design, per feature
- [`HierarchyCountsSample`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/HierarchyCountsSample.md)
  : Count distinct elements for each level of hierarchy per sample
- [`nr_children_experiment()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/nr_children_experiment.md)
  : Max nr_children across samples per hierarchy unit
- [`nr_features_experiment()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/nr_features_experiment.md)
  : Count distinct child features per hierarchy unit
- [`nr_obs_sample()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/nr_obs_sample.md)
  : Sum of observed children per hierarchy unit and sample
- [`summarize_stats_factors()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/summarize_stats_factors.md)
  : Compute variance, sd and related statistics for all factor levels
- [`which_missing()`](https://fgcz.github.io/prolfqua/reference/which_missing.md)
  : Draw missing values for an intensity vector based on its values
